=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- .claude/scripts/usage_limit_resumes.py:285-321 | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_8-flash, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, qwen_qwen3_7-plus]
  PROBLEM: The root selector uses a broad `startswith` check instead of the anchored resume-trigger pattern, so lookalike trigger names can be treated as pending resumes and block sessions indefinitely.
  WHY: The stale-routine sweep does not recognize or delete those lookalike names, leaving the session blocked; severity ranged from NIT to MAJOR, with MAJOR used here.
- .claude/scripts/usage_limit_resumes.py: entire file (481 lines vs twin's 489 lines) | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [qwen_qwen3_7-plus]
  PROBLEM: The root script lacks fire-offset constants and `fire_offset_minutes(position)`, so it does not space resume triggers.
  WHY: The pickup invokes the root script, which emits no per-entry fire offsets, causing resumed sessions to fire together instead of using the documented 4-every-3-minutes spacing.
- .claude/scripts/usage_limit_resumes.py:_skip_reason function (lines 347-373) | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [qwen_qwen3_7-plus]
  PROBLEM: The root script lacks `SESSION_WINDOW_HOURS` and the 72-hour cutoff check, so it does not emit the `too_old` skip reason.
  WHY: Sessions older than 72 hours can remain eligible and consume the per-wake quota ahead of recent stops.
- .claude/scripts/usage_limit_resumes.py:_load_entries function (lines 205-220) | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [qwen_qwen3_7-plus]
  PROBLEM: The root script does not handle a single `get_session` JSON payload with an `id` field but no `data` array.
  WHY: The pickup can pass its own session result as the first `--sessions` input, causing `InputError` and preventing the account-wide hold-off from firing.
- .claude/scripts/usage_limit_resumes.py:166-196 | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_8-flash, minimax_minimax-m3, qwen_qwen3_7-plus]
  PROBLEM: The root script’s JSON decoder does not distinguish exhausting `MAX_JSON_START_CANDIDATES` from finding no JSON object or array.
  WHY: Cap exhaustion and malformed input produce the same error, obscuring the cause of `limit_pending=unknown`; severity ranged from NIT to MAJOR, with MAJOR used here.
- .claude/scripts/usage_limit_resumes.py:135 | severity=low | confidence=[3]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro]
  PROBLEM: `LOGIN_PATTERN` allows consecutive and trailing hyphens and rejects logins containing dots.
  WHY: The accepted login shapes do not match GitHub’s username rules, although the reviewers report that the practical impact is near zero.
- workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/usage_limit_resumes.py:89 | severity=low | confidence=[3]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3, qwen_qwen3_7-plus]
  PROBLEM: `LOGIN_PATTERN` allows consecutive and trailing hyphens and rejects dotted logins.
  WHY: The pattern can accept invalid GitHub login shapes and reject valid ones, causing `InputError` and exit code 2 for affected handoff-author values.
- workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/usage_limit_resumes.py:362-378 | severity=low | confidence=[3]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: `_skip_reason` reports `too_old` rather than `not_idle:<status>` when a session is both non-IDLE and older than 72 hours.
  WHY: The skipped-list reason loses precision, potentially leading an operator to investigate the listing window instead of the session’s running status.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- .claude/scripts/usage_limit_resumes.py:321 (`is_resume = _text(trigger.get("name")).startswith(RESUME_TRIGGER_PREFIX)`) | severity=low | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The root selector uses `startswith("Resume after usage limit")` to detect resume triggers, while the twin and stale sweep require the anchored pattern `^Resume after usage limit \(`.
  WHY: A hand-named trigger `Resume after usage limit` (without opening paren) is treated as a pending resume by the root selector and blocks the session from being resumed, but the stale sweep never deletes it.
- .claude/scripts/usage_limit_resumes.py:135 (`LOGIN_PATTERN = re.compile(r"^[A-Za-z0-9](?:[A-Za-z0-9-]{0,38})(?:\[bot\])?$")`) | severity=low | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The character class `[A-Za-z0-9-]` allows consecutive hyphens and trailing hyphens, which GitHub username rules disallow. The regex also rejects logins containing dots.
  WHY: An operator setting `CLAUDE_FIXER_HANDOFF_AUTHOR_LOGIN` to a username with a trailing or consecutive hyphen (e.g. `a--b`, `a-`) would pass validation but the real GitHub login has those characters; the script exits 2 on a login that does not match, surfacing as `limit_pending=unknown`. The practical impact is near zero: the actual login used is `shubhodeep1` or `github-actions[bot]`, both of which match. The regex `{0,38}` upper bound is also 1 short of GitHub's 39-character username cap but this does not affect correctness.
=== END FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===

=== FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_8-flash ===
- .claude/scripts/usage_limit_resumes.py: line 321, is_resume = _text(trigger.get("name")).startswith(RESUME_TRIGGER_PREFIX) | severity=high | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The root script uses `startswith` with `RESUME_TRIGGER_PREFIX` instead of matching the anchored `RESUME_TRIGGER_NAME_PATTERN` regex used in the template twin, causing lookalike trigger names to be misclassified as active usage-limit resume triggers.
  WHY: If a bound trigger starts with "Resume after usage limit" without matching the exact pattern expected by `stale_routines.py`, `_wake_pending` treats it as a pending resume and skips the candidate session indefinitely, while `stale_routines.py` never cleans up the trigger.
- .claude/scripts/usage_limit_resumes.py: line 196, raise InputError(f"{path}: no JSON object or array found") | severity=low | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The root script does not report when candidate search reached the `MAX_JSON_START_CANDIDATES` ceiling in `_decode_json_text`, unlike the workflow-templates twin.
  WHY: For input files with large envelopes containing 50 or more non-JSON bracket starts before the payload, the function raises a generic error that conceals that the search ceiling was exhausted, making cap exhaustion indistinguishable from malformed JSON.

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/usage_limit_resumes.py:89 | severity=low | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The middle character class allows trailing hyphens (e.g. `name-`) and consecutive hyphens (e.g. `na--me`), which GitHub disallows for usernames.
  WHY: An operator who sets `CLAUDE_FIXER_HANDOFF_AUTHOR_LOGIN` to a username with a trailing or consecutive hyphen gets `InputError("--handoff-author-login must be a GitHub login (never empty)")` and exit code 2, surfacing as `limit_pending=unknown` on the pickup report. The current `test_login_must_be_a_github_login` only covers empty/whitespace/space/semicolon/leading-dash, so the regression slips through CI. The actual deployment value is typically a bot login (`github-actions[bot]`), so the blast radius is bounded, but the contract is wrong and a valid GitHub username can be rejected.
- workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/usage_limit_resumes.py:362-378 | severity=low | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: A session that is both `SESSION_STATUS_RUNNING` (or any non-IDLE status) and older than 72 hours is reported with reason `too_old` rather than the more specific `not_idle:<status>`.
  WHY: An operator investigating the pickup's `skipped` list sees `too_old` and may look for a listing-window bug, when the session is actually still running and the 72h cutoff is incidental. The order is documented in AD-21 as intentional ("age is a scope boundary"), but the test `test_sessions_created_more_than_72_hours_ago_are_skipped` only exercises IDLE sessions, so the conflict case is not pinned. Not a runtime bug; the report is the only thing that loses precision.
- .claude/scripts/usage_limit_resumes.py:181-193 (root copy, 481 lines) | severity=high | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: Two error paths in the active root script regress from the round-1 fixes that are present in the twin: `_bound_wakes` matches any trigger name starting with the literal prefix, and `_decode_json_text` raises `InputError(f"{path}: no JSON object or array found")` regardless of whether the scan hit `MAX_JSON_START_CANDIDATES`.
  WHY: The pickup invokes `.claude/scripts/usage_limit_resumes.py` (root), not the twin — the test setup at `tests/test_usage_limit_resumes.py:42-46` loads from `TEMPLATE_SCRIPT_PATH` precisely to make the active script look like the twin. The selector contract is "make no API call, output is the resume list"; an out-of-sync root means a hand-named trigger that no human will sweep keeps blocking its session forever. `tests/test_usage_limit_resumes.py::test_template_parity` will catch the divergence once the next sync runs, but until then the active runtime path is wrong. PR description and progress log both list this as expected pre-sync red; the PR carries a `hold` claim (comment 5922560221) until the sixth twin sync lands.
